metadata.goal: Investigate how vessel movement patterns vary across vessel types and between summer and winter.
metadata.header: Summer and Winter Vessel-Type Mobility Changes
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed Danish AIS-style North Sea case containing 131 complete cargo, ferry, and fishing trajectories in summer and winter, with static vessel attributes.
metadata.source_note: The geographic setting is west of Jutland; visible trajectories and seasonal relationships are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: Ferry and fishing traffic increases sharply during summer and remains much lower during winter, while cargo traffic shows less seasonal variation.

plot.title: Seasonal Traffic by Vessel Type
plot.description: Summer and winter distributions are compared separately for cargo, ferry, and fishing traffic.

insight_list.question: How do summer and winter movement counts differ among ferry, fishing, and cargo traffic?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Derive season from timestamp and compare trajectory-level measurements by ship_type.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path)
points['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(points['timestamp'])
points=points.merge(vessels,on='vessel_id')
points['season']=np.where(points.timestamp.dt.month.isin([6,7,8]),'summer','winter')
print(points.groupby(['season','ship_type']).trajectory_id.nunique())

insight_list.insight: Generally, in the summer months, the mean speeds of different vessel types are higher than in the winter months.
